value: can pass from parent birds to offspring (vertical spread)
occasional digestive or nervous system signs

mortality.value: can be fatal; the disease is described as potentially fatal in birds of any age

diagnosis.value: Post-mortem exam typically shows pneumonia, pleuritis and air sac inflammation; confirmed with lab tests such as bacterial culture, PCR, agar gel precipitation, ELISA or serum agglutination.

value: vaccination, reported to lower how often the disease occurs

treatment_overview.value: Antibiotics can be tried, chosen based on culture and sensitivity testing, but treatment does not always succeed.

summary.value: Ornithobacterium rhinotracheale (ORT) is a bacterium found worldwide that causes a potentially fatal respiratory illness in poultry of any age, spreading both bird-to-bird and from parent to chick. It is not known to infect humans, and while vaccination helps prevent it, antibiotic treatment is not always effective.
